members.name: SmoothingGroup
members.doc:
A 32-slot bitmask, the 3ds Max / ProBuilder model. Two smooth faces
share an averaged normal only when their masks intersect, so a cylinder
can keep its wall round while the cap stays flat without marking every
rim edge by hand. Zero is "ungrouped": ungrouped smooth faces smooth
against each other, which is what the old bare Smooth flag meant and
what every mesh authored before groups existed still decodes to.

members.name: PolyGroup
members.doc:
UE5's PolyGroup: a face partition that is neither the material slot nor
the smoothing group. Slots decide what a face is drawn with and groups
decide how it is shaded; a PolyGroup says which authored SURFACE the face
belongs to, which is what "select this whole panel" and "inset this
group" need on a mesh whose panels all share one material and one
smoothing group. Zero is ungrouped, so a mesh that never used them costs
nothing and reads back exactly as it was written.

members.name: Uvs
members.doc:
One UV per corner per channel, or empty. Empty channel 0 is
ProBuilder's "Auto UV": the projection above computes the coordinate
from world position, which is what keeps blockout fast and texel
density uniform for free. A non-empty list is "Manual UV" and overrides
the projection outright — it is what the unwrapper writes and what the
UV editor drags around. Channel 1 is the lightmap set: when empty it
resolves to channel 0, so a face without a dedicated lightmap layout
still has usable coordinates instead of zeros. The projection record
above is deliberately NOT per channel — an auto face has one world
projection, and a non-zero channel falls back through channel 0 to
reach it, so there is nothing for a second copy to describe.

types.name: FEditableMesh
types.doc:
A face-vertex mesh with a derived edge table, the representation ProBuilder
itself uses. Positions are welded, faces are corner-index lists into them,
and adjacency is rebuilt on demand. Hard edges cost nothing because the
render bake splits per face corner; a half-edge structure would buy O(1)
neighbour walks at the price of outlawing every non-manifold intermediate
state that extrude, bridge and detach legitimately pass through.

members.name: AddFace
members.signature: uint32_t AddFace(const std::vector<uint32_t>& indices, int32_t materialSlot = 0)

members.name: MarkTopologyDirty
members.doc:
Every structural operation ends here, which makes it the one place that
can guarantee the UV invariant. A face whose corner list changed size
loses its manual UVs rather than keeping a list that no longer lines up
— inert while the sizes disagree, but a trap the day a later edit makes
them match again by coincidence.

members.name: ExtrudeFacesAlong
members.signature: bool ExtrudeFacesAlong(const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, const Vec3& direction, std::vector<uint32_t>& outFaces)
members.doc:
Same walk as above but every new cap vertex moves along `direction`
instead of its own averaged normal, which is what an axis-locked
viewport drag needs: a face pushed along world +Y must stay in the plane
the gizmo is showing, not drift off along a bevelled normal.

members.name: ExtrudeEdges
members.signature: bool ExtrudeEdges(const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& edges, float distance, std::vector<FGeoEdge>& outEdges)

members.name: InsetFaces
members.signature: bool InsetFaces(const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, float amount, std::vector<uint32_t>& outFaces)

members.name: BevelEdges
members.signature: bool BevelEdges(const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& edges, float amount, uint32_t& outBeveled, uint32_t& outSkipped)

members.name: BevelEdges
members.signature: bool BevelEdges(const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& edges, float amount, int32_t segments, uint32_t& outBeveled, uint32_t& outSkipped)
members.doc:
The rounded form. Segments above 1 subdivide each bevel strip across the
edge and slerp the intermediate rows onto the arc around the original
vertex. The extra rows are spliced into the corner patch as well: the
strip's outermost row IS a patch boundary edge, so subdividing one
without the other opens a crack exactly at the corner the patch exists
to close.

members.name: BevelVertices
members.signature: bool BevelVertices(const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, float amount, int32_t segments, uint32_t& outBeveled, uint32_t& outSkipped)
members.doc:
Cuts the corner off a vertex: every incident edge gains a point `amount`
along it, each incident face swaps its corner for the two points its own
edges carry, and the ring of points closes as a cap. Segments above 1
dome that cap onto the sphere of radius `amount` around the original
vertex — the same slerp the rounded edge bevel uses on its strips, so a
vertex bevel and an edge bevel of the same amount meet on one surface
rather than a chamfer against a curve.

A boundary vertex is skipped: its incident faces do not close a fan, so
there is no ring for the cap to be, and guessing one folds the surface.

members.name: BakeManualUvs
members.doc:
Freeze the current projection into per-corner UVs, so the UV editor has
something to drag; the inverse drops back to the projection.

members.name: ActiveUvChannel
members.doc:
Which channel CornerUv, SetCornerUv, bake/clear and every FGeoUvOps /
FGeoUvUnwrap pass read and write. Editor view state, not mesh data: it
is never serialized, and Decode leaves it alone so an undo restore does
not yank the UV editor back to channel 0 mid-edit. The render bake
ignores it — the GPU vertex layout has one UV slot, fed from channel 0.

members.name: CornerUv
members.signature: Vec2 CornerUv(uint32_t faceIndex, uint32_t corner) const
members.doc:
The UV a corner resolves to on the active channel, whichever mode the
face is in: manual on the channel, else channel 0's manual layer, else
the projection.

members.signature: void SetEdgeSeam(const FGeoEdge& edge, bool seam)
members.doc:
Edges the unwrapper must not cross. Stored on the mesh rather than the
face because a seam belongs to the edge shared by two faces.

members.signature: void SetFaceMaterialSlot(const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, int32_t slot)

members.signature: void SetFaceSmooth(const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, bool smooth)

members.name: SetEdgeHard
members.signature: void SetEdgeHard(const FGeoEdge& edge, bool hard)
members.doc:
A crease the render bake never averages across, independent of the
smoothing groups: a group says which faces belong together, a hard edge
says where the surface breaks. Both are needed, because a single
smoothing group is the normal case for a whole object and the seam you
want is one edge inside it.

members.name: HasVertexColors
members.doc:
Per-vertex colour, allocated lazily. An empty array is not "black": it
is "no colours authored", and the bake emits opaque white for it, so a
mesh that never gets painted costs nothing and still lights correctly.

members.name: SetVertexColor
members.signature: void SetVertexColor(uint32_t vertex, const Vec4& color)

members.name: RepairTJunctions
members.doc:
Insert any vertex that sits on a face's edge but is not one of its
corners. A boolean split leaves exactly that: the seam edge of one
operand is subdivided by the other's planes, so it ends up shared by
three faces instead of two. The mesh is watertight either way, but the
T-junction shows as a shading seam and makes extrude and bevel walk the
wrong neighbour. Returns the number of corners inserted.

types.name: FGeoBakeMaterial
types.doc:
One surface as the bake writes it: the caller has already resolved the
material asset, so the codec never touches the asset system.

types.name: EGeoTangentSpace
types.doc:
How the bake fills LitVertex::tangent. Smoothed is what the render bake
already produces — accumulated across a shading partition, so a curved run
has one continuous frame. PerFace takes each triangle's own frame, which is
what a hard-surface bake with per-face normal maps wants; None leaves the
identity frame and is only for meshes with no normal map at all, where the
per-corner accumulation is measurable cost for nothing.

types.name: EGeoExportCollision
types.doc:
What collision setup the export authors beside the model. The result is a
`.mmeshmeta` sidecar in the mesh editor's own format, so a room exported with
a convex hull opens in the Static Mesh editor showing that hull and can be
refined there — the export is a starting point, not a second system.

members.name: GenerateLightmapUvs
members.doc:
Channel 1 gets its own non-overlapping layout. Padding is in TEXELS at
the stated resolution, because that is the number a lightmapper's bleed
is measured in; the unwrapper's margin is derived from the two.

members.name: ReplaceSourceAsset
members.doc:
Purely informational to the codec — the caller picks the path — but it is
recorded in the result so the panel can say which of the two it did
rather than guessing from the path it passed in.

types.name: FGeoMmodelBridge
types.doc:
The link between an imported `.mmodel` and the editable copy the UV editor
drags around. Without it a UV edit on an imported mesh could only ever be
saved as a NEW asset: nothing recorded which file vertex a given corner came
from, so the edit had to be re-baked and every reference to the original
left pointing at the old layout.

members.name: CornerBase
members.doc:
Per face: where its corners start in the three per-corner arrays below.
Sized FaceCount + 1, so a face's corner count is a subtraction.

members.name: IndexOfCorner
members.doc:
Which slot of its submesh's INDEX array this corner was read from. Only
the seam split needs it — splitting a vertex means pointing one corner's
index at the duplicate, and without this the write-back knows which file
vertex a corner came from but not which of that vertex's many references
to change.

members.name: VertexFileOffset
members.doc:
Per submesh: where its vertex and index blocks start in the FILE, and how
many records each holds. A UV-only write-back patches the vertex bytes in
place rather than re-serializing, so meshlets, LODs, the SDF grid and the
skeleton survive a UV edit untouched.

members.name: DataOffset
members.doc:
The two absolute offsets a split has to patch through: mesh entries carry
their vertex block relative to DataOffset, and the entry itself lives in
the table at MeshTableOffset.

members.name: SplitSourceVertices
members.doc:
Off refuses a torn seam and writes nothing, which is what a UV-only patch
must do: the file has one vertex where the edit now wants two, and
keeping either coordinate loses the other. On duplicates that file vertex
and re-points the corners, at the price of the derived blocks below.

members.name: Conflicts
members.doc:
Corners that disagreed across a shared file vertex. Non-zero with a
successful split too — it is how many tears were repaired, not how many
are outstanding.

members.name: DroppedMeshlets
members.doc:
A split invalidates the two derived blocks that carry their own copies of
the vertex data. They are not flagged, they are REMOVED: a flag can be
ignored and a zeroed block count cannot, and the runtime's fallback for a
model without them is the same path a pre-v4 / pre-v7 file takes.

types.name: FEditableMeshCodec
types.doc:
Text-safe round-trip for the editable topology. The blob is a compact
little-endian record stream; the scene stores it base64-encoded in one MDF
property, which keeps a shape that has never been edited out of the scene
file entirely (the component regenerates those from its parameters).

members.signature: static void Encode(const FEditableMesh& mesh, std::vector<uint8_t>& out)

members.name: Decode
members.signature: static bool Decode(const uint8_t* data, size_t size, FEditableMesh& out)

members.name: DecodeFromText
members.signature: static bool DecodeFromText(const std::string& text, FEditableMesh& out)

members.signature: static std::string Base64Encode(const uint8_t* data, size_t size)

members.name: BakeToMmodel
members.signature: static bool BakeToMmodel(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::string& absolutePath, const std::string& modelName, const FGeoBakeMaterial* materials, int32_t materialCount)
members.doc:
Writes a .mmodel v6 file (no skeleton, animation, meshlet or SDF
blocks) with one mesh entry per used material slot, so a built room
ships as an ordinary static-mesh asset while the editable form stays
on the component for further editing.

Slots carry resolved surfaces, not asset paths. The format's slot name
is 64 bytes; a `.mat` VFS path put there truncated silently, and the
real texture and colour fields sat at their defaults, so a re-imported
bake rendered plain white.

members.name: BakeToMmodel
members.signature: static bool BakeToMmodel(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::string& absolutePath, const std::string& modelName, const FGeoBakeMaterial* materials, int32_t materialCount, const FGeoExportOptions& options, FGeoExportResult& outResult)
members.doc:
The same bake with the export dialog's answers. The mesh is NOT mutated:
lightmap generation runs on a copy, because an export must never be able
to change the geometry the artist is still editing.

members.name: WriteCollisionSidecar
members.signature: static bool WriteCollisionSidecar(const FGeoRenderMesh& render, const std::string& modelAbsolutePath, EGeoExportCollision collision, int32_t hullVertices, std::string& outSidecarPath)
members.doc:
The `.mmeshmeta` half of the export, split out so the Static Mesh editor's
authored sockets and slot bindings survive a re-export: it loads whatever
is there, replaces only the collision block, and writes it back.

members.name: ImportMmodel
members.signature: static bool ImportMmodel(const std::string& absolutePath, FEditableMesh& outMesh, FGeoMmodelBridge& outBridge)
members.doc:
Reads a `.mmodel` into an editable mesh with WELDED positions and the
file's own per-corner UVs on both channels, recording the corner -> file
vertex map that WriteBackUvs needs. Positions weld and UVs do not: that
is the whole point — a seam in the source stays a seam.

members.name: ImportMmodel
members.signature: static bool ImportMmodel(const std::string& absolutePath, FEditableMesh& outMesh, FGeoMmodelBridge& outBridge, std::vector<FGeoBakeMaterial>* outMaterials)
members.doc:
The same import, also handing back the file's material entries in the
model's own slot order. The UV editor's texture backdrop needs them: an
imported mesh has no component to read a material path off, and re-reading
the file a second time to find one would be a second answer to the same
question. `outMaterials` may be null.

members.name: WriteBackUvs
members.signature: static bool WriteBackUvs(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoMmodelBridge& bridge, uint32_t channel, uint32_t& outConflicts)
members.doc:
Writes one UV channel back into the file the bridge came from, patching
only the UV bytes. Returns false and writes NOTHING when two corners that
share a file vertex now disagree — the edit tore a UV seam the source
model has no vertex split for, and silently keeping one of the two would
lose half the work. `outConflicts` says how many, so the caller can offer
a re-bake instead.

members.name: WriteBackUvs
members.signature: static bool WriteBackUvs(const FEditableMesh& mesh, FGeoMmodelBridge& bridge, uint32_t channel, const FGeoUvWriteBackOptions& options, FGeoUvWriteBackResult& outResult)
members.doc:
The same write-back with the option to split the source model's vertices
instead of refusing a torn seam. The bridge is taken by REFERENCE and
updated in place: a split changes which file vertex a corner resolves to,
and a stale bridge would send the next channel's save to the vertex the
corner used to share.

What the split costs, honestly: the duplicated vertex block is appended
at the end of the file and the mesh entry re-pointed at it, so positions,
the SDF grid, the GI card set, the node tree, the materials and the
skeleton are all still valid — none of them names a vertex index. The two
blocks that DO are removed rather than left stale: the meshlet remap
shares one vertex between the corners the split just separated, and a
cooked LOD carries its own copy of the UVs the edit changed. Both fall
back to the runtime path a model without them has always taken, and a
re-cook rebuilds them.

members.name: edited
members.doc:
Non-zero once an operation has changed the topology away from what the
parameters above generate. Only then does the scene carry the full
topology blob; a pristine shape reloads from its parameters.

members.name: useBakedModel
members.doc:
Render from the baked .mmodel instead of regenerating the mesh at load.
The bake only paid off once something consumed it: the file was written
and then ignored, so a packaged build still re-triangulated every room
on the way in. With this on the mesh comes through the normal asset
path, which is also what gets meshlets and LODs once the cook learns to
reprocess .mmodel.

members.name: interactive
members.doc:
Set while a viewport drag is in flight. The render mesh still rebuilds
every frame so the edit is visible, but the collider does not: rebuilding
it means handing Jolt a new mesh shape per frame, which is the single
most expensive thing in the loop and is worthless mid-drag.

members.name: undecodedTopology
members.doc:
Topology this build could not decode — a newer schema, or a damaged
blob. Held verbatim so the next save writes it back untouched: dropping
to the shape parameters renders something, but re-saving would then
replace the author's geometry with a default primitive, permanently.

members.name: Apply
members.signature: static bool Apply(EGeoBooleanOp op, const FEditableMesh& subject, const Mat4& subjectToWorld, const FEditableMesh& tool, const Mat4& toolToWorld, FEditableMesh& outResult, std::string& outError)
members.doc:
`subject` and `tool` are each in their own local space; the matrices put
them in a shared space, and the result is returned in `subject` space so
the edited entity's transform stays untouched.

Returns false and fills outError when either operand is empty, not a
closed solid, or the result would be degenerate — a boolean against an
open shell has no defined inside, and silently producing garbage is
worse than refusing.

members.name: WeldThreshold
members.doc:
Distance under which two boolean-produced vertices are the same vertex.
Splits land on shared planes, so the duplicates are numerically close
rather than arbitrary.

members.name: Seed
members.doc:
The seed is part of the authored data, not a clock read: a displace that
gave a different rock every time the panel was pressed could never be
re-applied after an undo, and the room would drift on every reload.

types.name: FGeoLattice
types.doc:
The control grid a lattice deform runs through. Held apart from the options
that shape it so a viewport tool can drag the points directly and call
ApplyLattice with the same code path the panel's profile uses.

members.name: ControlIndex
members.signature: uint32_t ControlIndex(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z) const

types.name: EGeoLatticeProfile
types.doc:
The four shaping profiles, each reachable as a handle sitting ON the lattice
rather than as a number in a panel. A profile is a function of position along
the lattice axis, so its handle belongs at the end of that axis where the
effect is largest and the drag reads as the deformation itself.

members.name: Axis
members.doc:
0/1/2 — the axis the profile runs along. Everything below is a function
of the normalized distance along it.

members.name: BuildLattice
members.signature: static bool BuildLattice(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const FGeoLatticeOptions& options, FGeoLattice& out)
members.doc:
Bounds-fitted control grid over `vertices` (or the whole mesh when
empty). Deformed starts equal to Rest, so applying an unshaped lattice is
a no-op rather than a collapse.

members.name: ShapeLattice
members.signature: static void ShapeLattice(FGeoLattice& lattice, const FGeoLatticeOptions& options)
members.doc:
Moves the control points by the authored profile. Every term is a
function of the point's own position along the lattice axis, which is
what makes twist, bend and taper compose in any order without the
sequence mattering.

members.name: ApplyLattice
members.signature: static uint32_t ApplyLattice(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const FGeoLattice& lattice)
members.doc:
Trilinear over the control DISPLACEMENTS, not the control positions: a
vertex under an unshaped cell must not move at all, and interpolating
positions in a lattice coarser than the mesh quantizes it onto the grid.

members.name: Lattice
members.signature: static uint32_t Lattice(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const FGeoLatticeOptions& options)

members.name: PickLatticeControl
members.signature: static uint32_t PickLatticeControl(const FGeoLattice& lattice, const Mat4& viewProjection, const Vec2& viewportSize, const Vec2& screen, float radiusPixels)
members.doc:
`viewProjection` already carries the object matrix, so the lattice never
has to know it sits under a transform. Returns kGeoLatticeNoControl when
nothing is within `radiusPixels`; ties go to the point nearest the camera,
which is what makes the front face of the cage clickable at all.

members.name: MoveLatticeControl
members.signature: static void MoveLatticeControl(FGeoLattice& lattice, uint32_t control, const Vec3& delta)

members.name: GatherLatticeEdges
members.signature: static void GatherLatticeEdges(const FGeoLattice& lattice, std::vector<uint32_t>& outPairs)
members.doc:
The cage's wireframe as a flat list of index pairs — the twelve-ish runs
between adjacent controls. Flat because a vector of pairs would have the
caller unpacking a type it does not otherwise need.

members.name: LatticeProfileHandle
members.signature: static Vec3 LatticeProfileHandle(const FGeoLattice& lattice, const FGeoLatticeOptions& options, EGeoLatticeProfile profile)
members.doc:
Where a profile's handle sits, in the lattice's own space. Twist and taper
sit on the far end's rim (on the two perpendicular axes, so neither steals
the other's click), bend on the far end's centre and bulge on the waist —
the point each one actually moves the most.

members.name: LatticeProfileFromDrag
members.signature: static float LatticeProfileFromDrag(const FGeoLattice& lattice, const FGeoLatticeOptions& options, EGeoLatticeProfile profile, float startValue, const Vec3& delta)
members.doc:
The value a drag of that handle means. Twist and bend come back as the
angle actually swept about the lattice centre (a drag of one radius
tangentially is 45 degrees, not a made-up gain), taper and bulge as a
fraction of the half extent the handle stands on.

members.name: LatticeProfileValue
members.signature: static float LatticeProfileValue(const FGeoLatticeOptions& options, EGeoLatticeProfile profile)

members.name: SetLatticeProfileValue
members.signature: static void SetLatticeProfileValue(FGeoLatticeOptions& options, EGeoLatticeProfile profile, float value)

members.name: Displace
members.signature: static uint32_t Displace(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const FGeoDisplaceOptions& options)

members.name: Smooth
members.signature: static uint32_t Smooth(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, int32_t iterations, float strength, bool preserveBoundary)
members.doc:
Laplacian relaxation. Boundary vertices are pinned when asked, because
the alternative is a shell that shrinks away from every open edge each
time the tool is pressed.

members.name: SampleNoise
members.signature: static float SampleNoise(const Vec3& position, uint32_t seed)
members.doc:
Deterministic value noise in [-1, 1]. Public because the panel's preview
and the op have to agree, and a second implementation would not.

free.name: kGeoLatticeNoControl
free.doc:
No control point under the cursor. A sentinel rather than a bool-plus-index
pair because the pick result is stored on the tool between events and a stale
index paired with a false flag is the classic way one gets dragged anyway.

types.name: EGeoExtrudeMode
types.doc:
Group is one cap over the whole selection, with interior edges left welded
— the standard "push this wall out". Individual gives every face its own
cap and its own four walls, which is how a row of windows gets pushed out of
a facade without the gaps between them closing up.

members.name: Depth
members.doc:
Positive pushes the inner face out along its normal, negative sinks it.
Inset plus depth in one operation is what makes a panel or a recessed
window a single step instead of inset-then-extrude-then-reselect.

members.name: Individual
members.doc:
False insets the outline of the whole selected region, so a 2x2 block of
faces gets one border rather than four. True insets each face.

types.name: FGeoSoftSelection
types.doc:
A weighted vertex set. The viewport tool builds one on mouse-down and reuses
it for every frame of the drag: recomputing the falloff per frame would let
the influence region crawl as the vertices move.

types.name: EGeoKnifeSnap
types.doc:
What a knife point locked onto. The viewport draws the snap it got rather
than the snap it asked for, because a point that silently failed to land on
the midpoint it was hovering is the difference between a symmetric cut and a
cut that is one pixel off on every segment.

types.name: FGeoKnifeOptions
types.doc:
The knife's whole view of the camera: one matrix and a viewport size. Keeping
it to that is what lets the stroke be replayed headlessly — the op never sees
a camera object, so a test can hand it any projection it likes.

members.name: Closed
members.doc:
Closes the polyline back onto its first point, which is how a window is
cut out of a wall in one gesture.

members.name: CutThrough
members.doc:
False keeps the cut on the faces whose projected winding faces the
camera, so a stroke over a box cuts the near wall only. True cuts every
face under the stroke, the "cut through" every modeller offers.

members.name: PlaneOffset
members.doc:
The plane is dot(Normal, P) == Offset, so a mirror about the object's
own YZ plane is the default and needs no extra setup.

members.name: Duplicate
members.doc:
False reflects the mesh in place (a flip); true appends the reflection
and keeps the original, which is the symmetry-modelling case.

members.name: TargetRatio
members.doc:
Fraction of the current triangle count to keep. 1 is a no-op, 0.25 is the
usual "make this blockout cheap enough to place a hundred of".

members.name: PreserveBoundary
members.doc:
A boundary edge and a material border are both places where a collapse
changes something the quadric cannot see — the silhouette of an open
shell, and which submesh a triangle lands in. Both are locked by default
because the damage is invisible in the viewport and obvious in the bake.

members.name: MaxError
members.doc:
Above this quadric error a collapse is refused however much budget is
left, so a target ratio that cannot be reached without wrecking the shape
stops early instead. Zero is unbounded.

types.name: EGeoProjectMode
types.doc:
How a projection finds the point on the target it moves a vertex to. Normal
casts along the vertex normal, which keeps a wall's own layout when it is
pushed onto a terrain; Closest takes the nearest surface point outright,
which is what shrink-wrapping a proxy onto a detailed mesh wants.

members.name: MaxDistance
members.doc:
Vertices further than this from any target surface are left alone, so a
projection over a partial target does not suck the rest of the mesh into
it. Zero is unbounded.

members.name: Blend
members.doc:
0 leaves the mesh where it is, 1 lands it on the target. Anything between
is the "ease it down" pass every terrain-fitting workflow uses.

members.name: Rays
members.doc:
Rays per vertex over the cosine-weighted hemisphere. The set is a fixed
Hammersley sequence, not random: an AO bake that changed with every press
could not be undone to the same mesh it came from.

members.name: Radius
members.doc:
Occlusion beyond this distance does not count, which is what stops a
room's own floor darkening every wall to black.

members.name: Bias
members.doc:
Ray origins are pushed off the surface by this much. Without it a ray
leaving a vertex re-hits one of the faces that vertex belongs to and
every vertex bakes fully occluded.

members.name: OnProgress
members.doc:
Called every few vertices with how many are done; returning false stops
the bake. A stopped bake has already written the vertices it finished,
so a caller that may stop it bakes a copy of the mesh.

members.name: Multiply
members.doc:
Multiplies into whatever colour is already there rather than replacing
it, so an AO bake over a painted mesh darkens the paint instead of
erasing a day of work.

members.name: ExtrudeFaces
members.signature: static bool ExtrudeFaces(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, const FGeoExtrudeOptions& options, std::vector<uint32_t>& outFaces)

members.name: InsetFaces
members.signature: static bool InsetFaces(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, const FGeoInsetOptions& options, std::vector<uint32_t>& outFaces)

members.name: EdgeRing
members.signature: static std::vector<FGeoEdge> EdgeRing(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoEdge& seed)
members.doc:
The edge walks a loop cut is built on, and the two selection commands a
level artist reaches for constantly. A ring crosses quads (the edges a
loop cut would sever); a loop runs along them through 4-valence
vertices. Both stop at the first face that is not a quad rather than
guessing, because a guessed ring cuts the wrong thing silently.

members.name: EdgeLoop
members.signature: static std::vector<FGeoEdge> EdgeLoop(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoEdge& seed)

members.name: InsertEdgeLoop
members.signature: static bool InsertEdgeLoop(FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoEdge& seed, float position, int32_t cuts, std::vector<FGeoEdge>& outEdges)
members.doc:
Inserts `cuts` parallel loops across the ring the seed edge belongs to.
`position` is where a single cut lands along the seed edge (0.5 is the
midpoint); with more than one cut the loops are spaced evenly and the
position is ignored, matching every other modeller.

members.name: SubdivideEdges
members.signature: static bool SubdivideEdges(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& edges, int32_t cuts, std::vector<uint32_t>& outVertices)
members.doc:
Splits the given edges without cutting the faces: every face touching a
split edge absorbs the new corners. That leaves n-gons rather than a
T-junction, which is the difference between geometry that still bevels
correctly and geometry that shades with a visible crack.

members.name: PlaneCut
members.signature: static bool PlaneCut(FEditableMesh& mesh, const Vec3& planeNormal, float planeOffset, EGeoCutMode mode, bool fillCap, std::vector<FGeoEdge>& outCutEdges)
members.doc:
The knife, expressed as a plane rather than a screen-space stroke: the
stroke is the viewport tool's job, and every stroke reduces to a plane
through the camera anyway. `outCutEdges` is the seam the cut produced,
which is what a follow-up bevel or extrude selects.

members.name: KnifeCut
members.signature: static bool KnifeCut(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<Vec2>& screenPath, const FGeoKnifeOptions& options, std::vector<FGeoEdge>& outCutEdges)
members.doc:
The screen-space knife. Each segment of the polyline becomes its own
plane — the one through the camera and the two screen points — applied
ONLY to the faces that segment crosses in screen space. A single plane
over the whole stroke is what PlaneCut already is, and it cuts the far
side of the model as well as the near one, which is exactly what a knife
must not do. Faces the cut does not touch still absorb the vertices it
put on their shared edges, so the result has no T-junctions.

members.name: SnapKnifePoint
members.signature: static FGeoKnifeHit SnapKnifePoint(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoKnifeOptions& options, const Vec2& screen)
members.doc:
Where a knife point actually lands. Vertices win over edge midpoints and
midpoints over the edge itself, so a deliberate corner cut is not stolen
by the midpoint two pixels away.

members.name: ProjectToScreen
members.signature: static bool ProjectToScreen(const Mat4& viewProjection, const Vec2& viewportSize, const Vec3& point, Vec2& outScreen)
members.doc:
Mesh-local screen position of a vertex, or false when it is behind the
camera. Exposed because the viewport preview has to draw the same points
the cut will use, and a second projection drifts from this one.

members.name: ConformNormals
members.doc:
Makes every face's winding agree with its neighbours', then orients the
whole shell outward by signed volume. Returns the number of faces
flipped. A boolean result or a hand-bridged patch is the usual source of
a mesh that renders with holes from one side only.

members.name: AutoSmooth
members.signature: static uint32_t AutoSmooth(FEditableMesh& mesh, float angleDegrees)
members.doc:
Marks every edge whose dihedral angle exceeds the threshold hard and
smooths everything else — the one-click answer to "why is my cylinder
faceted". Returns the number of edges creased.

members.name: SetEdgeHardness
members.signature: static void SetEdgeHardness(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& edges, bool hard)

members.name: Triangulate
members.signature: static uint32_t Triangulate(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces)

members.name: Quadrangulate
members.signature: static uint32_t Quadrangulate(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, float angleDegrees)
members.doc:
Fuses adjacent triangle pairs back into quads when the pair is
near-planar and the quad it would make is convex. Returns the number of
pairs merged. Anything left over stays a triangle: a forced quad that
folds along its diagonal shades worse than the two triangles did.

The pairing is a maximum-weight matching approached by a weight-ordered
seed followed by bounded alternating-path augmentation, not the plain
greedy it used to be: greedy takes the flattest pair first and never
gives it back, so a strip of triangles reliably ended with an odd one out
that a single swap two pairs earlier would have absorbed.

members.name: MergeFaces
members.signature: static bool MergeFaces(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, float angleDegrees, uint32_t& outFace)
members.doc:
Fuses a connected, coplanar face selection into one n-gon. Refuses a
selection whose boundary is not a single loop — a merged face with a
hole in it has no valid corner list — and one whose faces bend away from
the selection's average normal by more than `angleDegrees`: an n-gon that
is not planar triangulates differently every time its corner order
changes, so the merge would show as a shading crease that moves.

members.name: FillHoles
members.signature: static uint32_t FillHoles(FEditableMesh& mesh, std::vector<uint32_t>& outFaces)
members.doc:
Caps every boundary loop. A pinch vertex — one where two loops meet at a
single corner — is walked by turning as tightly as possible in the
surface's own plane rather than refused, so an hourglass hole caps as the
two holes it is instead of leaving the whole mesh open.

members.name: Mirror
members.signature: static bool Mirror(FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoMirrorOptions& options, uint32_t& outWelded)

members.name: BuildSoftSelection
members.signature: static void BuildSoftSelection(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& seeds, float radius, EGeoFalloff falloff, FGeoSoftSelection& out)
members.doc:
Distances are measured along edges, not through space: a soft selection
that leaked through the gap in a folded surface would drag the far side
of the fold with it.

members.name: TranslateSoft
members.signature: static void TranslateSoft(FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoSoftSelection& selection, const Vec3& delta)

members.name: PaintVertices
members.signature: static void PaintVertices(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const Vec4& color, float strength)

members.name: PaintSoft
members.signature: static void PaintSoft(FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoSoftSelection& selection, const Vec4& color, float strength)

members.name: PaintFaces
members.signature: static void PaintFaces(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, const Vec4& color)

members.name: SimplifyMesh
members.signature: static uint32_t SimplifyMesh(FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoSimplifyOptions& options)
members.doc:
Quadric edge collapse to a triangle budget. The mesh is TRIANGULATED
first: a quadric is defined per plane, and an n-gon that is not planar
has no single plane to contribute — every simplifier makes the same
trade, and quadrangulate is the way back. Per-face material slots and
PolyGroups survive on the faces that survive; manual per-corner UVs do
not, because a corner that moved to a quadric-optimal position has no
coordinate that was ever authored for it. Returns the collapses applied.

members.name: ProjectToTarget
members.signature: static uint32_t ProjectToTarget(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const FEditableMesh& target, const FGeoProjectOptions& options)
members.doc:
Moves each vertex onto another mesh's surface. Directions and distances
are measured against the target BEFORE anything moves, so the result does
not depend on the vertex order — the same defect the displace deformer
had to avoid. Returns the number of vertices moved.

members.name: BakeVertexAmbientOcclusion
members.signature: static uint32_t BakeVertexAmbientOcclusion(FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoAmbientOcclusionOptions& options)
members.doc:
Ray-cast ambient occlusion into the vertex colours. Brute force against
the mesh's own triangles with a bounding-sphere reject per face — the
meshes this tool edits are blockout, and a BVH here would be a second
acceleration structure to keep correct for a bake that runs once.

members.name: AutoPolyGroups
members.signature: static uint32_t AutoPolyGroups(FEditableMesh& mesh, float angleDegrees)
members.doc:
PolyGroups: UE5's face partition, independent of both the material slot
and the smoothing group. AutoPolyGroups floods across edges the surface
does not bend more than `angleDegrees` at and numbers each region from 1,
which is the one-click way to get a blockout's panels named.

members.name: SetPolyGroup
members.signature: static void SetPolyGroup(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, uint32_t group)

members.name: FacesInPolyGroup
members.signature: static std::vector<uint32_t> FacesInPolyGroup(const FEditableMesh& mesh, uint32_t group)

members.name: SelectPolyGroupConnected
members.signature: static std::vector<uint32_t> SelectPolyGroupConnected(const FEditableMesh& mesh, uint32_t seedFace)
members.doc:
The group under a seed face, walked through adjacency rather than taken
from the whole mesh: two panels that happen to carry the same id are two
selections, and merging them on a click would be a silent join.

members.name: PolyGroupBoundaryEdges
members.doc:
Every edge whose two faces sit in different groups — what a PolyGroup
overlay draws, and what a group-aware inset uses as its outline.

members.signature: static std::vector<uint32_t> FacesWithMaterial(const FEditableMesh& mesh, int32_t slot)

members.signature: static std::vector<uint32_t> SelectCoplanarConnected(const FEditableMesh& mesh, uint32_t seedFace, float angleDegrees)

Appended, never inserted: the value is what a scene stores, so slotting
a new shape into the middle would silently re-type every placed brush

free.name: kGeoUvChannels

anything else that needs a unique, non-overlapping layout.

types.name: GeometryMeshSystem
types.doc:
Keeps every EditableMeshComponent's render mesh and collider in step with
its topology. Parameter edits in the Details panel regenerate the shape;
a tool operation bumps the component's revision and only the render bake
re-runs, so a 10k-vert room does not get re-generated from parameters it
no longer matches.

members.name: BakeToAsset
members.signature: bool BakeToAsset(EntityID entity, const std::string& absolutePath, const std::string& vfsPath)
members.doc:
Writes the current topology to `absolutePath` as a .mmodel and records
`vfsPath` on the component. The editable form stays untouched, so the
room can keep being edited after it has been baked for shipping.

members.name: ResolveBakeMaterial
members.signature: static FGeoBakeMaterial ResolveBakeMaterial(const std::string& materialPath, int32_t slot)
members.doc:
Public because the UV editor resolves the same surface to find the
albedo it draws under the layout — one resolver, not two answers.

types.name: FGeoShapeParams
types.doc:
The authored parameter set every generator reads. One struct for all
shapes keeps the reflected component flat, so the Details panel edits a
stair's step count and a torus's ring count through the same fields.

members.name: OpeningWidth
members.doc:
The doorway cut out of the Door shape's wall panel, in world units
rather than a fraction of Size, so resizing the wall does not resize the
hole a level's whole art set has to fit through.

types.name: EGeoSnapTarget
types.doc:
What an element drag lands on. Grid is the caller's step snapping; the other
three snap onto real geometry, which is the only way to get two blockout
pieces genuinely flush instead of visually close.

types.name: FGeometrySnap
types.doc:
Axis-constrained snapping for element drags. A drag moves a selection along
one axis, so every candidate reduces to a single number: the delta at which
the selection's pivot lines up with that piece of geometry. Vertices and
edge midpoints project onto the axis; a surface contributes the delta at
which the pivot lands on its plane, which is what makes a dragged face come
out flush rather than near.

members.name: AppendDeltas
members.signature: static void AppendDeltas(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const Mat4& toPivotSpace, const std::vector<bool>& excluded, EGeoSnapTarget target, const Vec3& pivot, const Vec3& axis, std::vector<float>& outDeltas)
members.doc:
Appends candidates from one mesh. `toPivotSpace` maps the mesh's own
space into the space the pivot and axis live in. `excluded` marks the
vertices being dragged — a selection that snapped to itself would pin
the moment the drag started; pass an empty span for other meshes.

members.name: Resolve
members.signature: static bool Resolve(const std::vector<float>& deltas, float rawDelta, float tolerance, float& outDelta)
members.doc:
Nearest candidate to `rawDelta` within `tolerance`. False leaves the
drag free, which is what keeps geometry snapping usable in open space.

members.name: Axis
members.doc: Object-space axis through the pivot: 0 = X, 1 = Y, 2 = Z.

members.name: BendDegrees
members.doc: The whole path turns this far, toward BendToward, along a circular arc.

members.name: EndScale
members.doc: The cross-section's scale at the far end; 1 keeps it constant.

members.name: SelectionBounds
members.doc:
Every element lands on the selection's own min / centre / max: the
flatten that lines a ragged edge up.

members.name: Pivot
members.doc:
The elements move rigidly until their min / centre / max sits on the
object's pivot plane: "drop to floor" is Y, Min, Pivot.

members.name: Revolve
members.signature: static uint32_t Revolve(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& profile, const FGeoRevolveOptions& options)
members.doc:
Sweeps a profile made of `profile` (or, when empty, every open boundary
edge of the mesh) around the axis. A full turn closes on itself and
shares the first ring instead of duplicating it; a vertex on the axis is
shared by every step, so a profile that touches the axis closes into a
cap rather than a ring of zero-area quads. The new faces face away from
the axis. Returns the number of faces added.

members.name: SweepPath
members.signature: static bool SweepPath(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, const FGeoPathOptions& options)
members.doc:
Extrudes the faces as one group, Segments times, and places each new
cap on the path: along the selection's normal, turning toward
BendToward by BendDegrees over the whole length, twisting and scaling
as it goes. The caps keep their face indices, as an extrude does.

members.name: Xform
members.signature: static bool Xform(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const FGeoXformOptions& options)
members.doc:
Translate, rotate (the engine's euler order, as TransformComponent
composes it) and scale about the pivot.
`vertices` empty means the whole mesh.

members.name: XformMatrix
members.signature: static Mat4 XformMatrix(const Vec3& pivot, const FGeoXformOptions& options)

members.name: Align
members.signature: static bool Align(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& vertices, const FGeoAlignOptions& options)
members.doc:
`vertices` empty means the whole mesh; SelectionBounds then has nothing
to flatten against and returns false.

members.name: PivotPoint
members.signature: static Vec3 PivotPoint(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& selection, EGeoPivotLocation location)
members.doc:
The object-space point a pivot moves to. Moving it is the caller's job:
every vertex shifts by minus this point and the owner's transform by
the same point in its own space, so nothing moves in the world.

members.name: BoundaryEdges
members.doc: Every open boundary edge, as the profile a bare Revolve takes.

types.name: FGeoUvTopology
types.doc:
The corner -> UV-vertex weld map. Storage is per-corner, so "these corners
are one point in UV space" is a derived fact: corners weld when they share
the 3D vertex AND their UVs coincide within epsilon. Every island walk, sew,
weld and relax needs this map; building it once per mesh revision replaces
the O(F^2 * C^2) coincidence scans the UV editor used to do per click.

members.name: Build
members.signature: static void Build(const FEditableMesh& mesh, float epsilon, FGeoUvTopology& out)

members.name: UvVertex
members.signature: uint32_t UvVertex(uint32_t face, uint32_t corner) const

members.name: UvArea
members.doc: Signed-area sums, so a mirrored chart still reports its real coverage.

members.name: TexelDensity
members.doc:
sqrt(UvArea / WorldArea): UV units per world unit. Multiply by the
texture edge in pixels to get px/m, the number artists actually match.

types.name: FGeoUdimTile
types.doc:
One UDIM tile with something in it. The number is the Mari/Substance
convention — 1001 + u + v * 10 — because that is what every texturing tool
names its files by, and a tile grid that numbered itself differently would
be unusable the moment the textures came back.

types.name: FGeoUvOps
types.doc:
UV-space operations over the manual-UV layer. Every mutating op bakes the
affected faces to manual first — running any of these against a live
projection would write coordinates the projection immediately recomputes.

members.name: BuildIslands
members.signature: static uint32_t BuildIslands(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const FGeoUvTopology& topology, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, std::vector<uint32_t>& outIslandPerFace)
members.doc:
Islands by actual UV connectivity (shared welded UV vertices), not by
dihedral angle: what BuildCharts predicts, this measures. One entry per
mesh face; faces outside `faces` (when non-empty) get 0xFFFFFFFF.

members.name: GatherIslandInfo
members.signature: static void GatherIslandInfo(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& islandPerFace, uint32_t islandCount, std::vector<FGeoUvIslandInfo>& out)

members.name: MarkOverlaps
members.signature: static void MarkOverlaps(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& islandPerFace, std::vector<FGeoUvIslandInfo>& islands, uint32_t maxTrianglePairs = 262144)
members.doc:
Marks islands whose triangles genuinely cross (SAT per triangle pair,
bbox-gated). Capped: past `maxTrianglePairs` the test degrades to the
bbox answer rather than stalling the editor on a dense mesh.

members.name: SewEdges
members.signature: static uint32_t SewEdges(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& edges)
members.doc:
Joins the two UV copies of each edge (average per endpoint, written to
both faces) and clears its seam flag. Returns edges sewn; an edge not
shared by exactly two faces is skipped.

members.name: SplitEdges
members.signature: static uint32_t SplitEdges(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<FGeoEdge>& edges)
members.doc:
The topological inverse of Sew: the corners stay put, but the edge
becomes a seam so island walks and the unwrapper treat the sides apart.

members.name: WeldCorners
members.signature: static uint32_t WeldCorners(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<FGeoUvCornerRef>& corners, float threshold)
members.doc:
Merges the selected corners that sit on the same 3D vertex and lie
within `threshold` of each other in UV space onto their average.

members.name: Straighten
members.signature: static bool Straighten(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<FGeoUvCornerRef>& corners)
members.doc:
Projects the selected corners onto their best-fit line (principal axis
of the 2D covariance), which straightens a border run without forcing
it onto U or V.

members.name: Relax
members.signature: static uint32_t Relax(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, uint32_t iterations, float alpha)
members.doc:
Laplacian smoothing of the subject faces' UVs. Island-boundary UV
vertices are pinned, so the outline holds while the interior evens out.

members.name: PackIslands
members.signature: static bool PackIslands(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, float margin, bool allowRotate)
members.doc:
Re-packs the subject's islands into the 0-1 square, preserving each
island's internal layout and their relative scale. `allowRotate` turns
a tall island 90 degrees when that makes it wider than high, which is
what lets shelf packing approach a MaxRects fill.

members.name: UdimNumber
members.signature: static uint32_t UdimNumber(int32_t u, int32_t v)
members.doc:
UDIM. Coordinates outside the 0-1 square are not an error to be clamped
away — they are how a character with four 4K sheets is laid out — so
every op above leaves them alone and these are what make them legible.

members.name: UdimFromNumber
members.signature: static bool UdimFromNumber(uint32_t number, int32_t& outU, int32_t& outV)

members.name: TileOfFace
members.signature: static bool TileOfFace(const FEditableMesh& mesh, uint32_t face, int32_t& outU, int32_t& outV)
members.doc:
Which tile a face sits in, by its UV centroid: a face straddling a tile
border belongs to the tile most of it is in, which is the only answer
that keeps "select this tile" from returning overlapping sets.

members.name: GatherUdimTiles
members.signature: static uint32_t GatherUdimTiles(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, std::vector<FGeoUdimTile>& out)

members.name: FacesInTile
members.signature: static std::vector<uint32_t> FacesInTile(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, int32_t u, int32_t v)

members.name: MoveFacesToTile
members.signature: static uint32_t MoveFacesToTile(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, int32_t u, int32_t v)
members.doc:
Translates the subject by WHOLE tiles, so its layout inside the tile is
untouched. Fractional-offset moves are what the drag already does; this
is the one that has to be exact, because a tile assignment that drifted
by a texel would sample the neighbouring sheet along one edge.

members.name: ComputeTexelDensity
members.signature: static float ComputeTexelDensity(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces)

members.name: SetTexelDensity
members.signature: static uint32_t SetTexelDensity(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, float targetDensity)
members.doc: Scales each island about its own centre until it hits `targetDensity`.

members.name: EqualizeTexelDensity
members.signature: static uint32_t EqualizeTexelDensity(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces)
members.doc:
Scales every island to the subject's area-weighted average density —
the "equalize" that makes one texture read uniformly across a room.

members.name: AngleThresholdDegrees
members.doc:
Faces whose shared edge bends by more than this are cut apart. 45 is
the hard-surface default: it keeps a curved run together and splits a
box into six charts without any hand-marked seam.

members.name: Margin
members.doc:
Gutter between charts, as a fraction of the 0-1 square. Two charts
closer than a texel bleed into each other under bilinear filtering and
again at every mip.

members.name: PreserveRelativeScale
members.doc:
Keep each chart at its world scale relative to the others, so a wall
twice the size gets twice the texture area. Off packs every chart to
the same size, which wastes resolution on small faces but maximises
the space each one gets.

members.name: Coverage
members.doc:
Fraction of the 0-1 square the charts actually cover. Low numbers mean
the shelf packer left gutters a smarter packer would have used.

types.name: FGeoUvUnwrap
types.doc:
Angle-based charting with a planar projection per chart and shelf packing
into the 0-1 square — the same shape as Blender's Smart UV Project. Not
conformal: a chart that is not developable keeps the distortion its best-fit
plane gives it. For blockout and hard-surface that is the right trade, and
it is deterministic, which an iterative solver is not.

members.name: Unwrap
members.signature: static FGeoUnwrapResult Unwrap(FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, const FGeoUnwrapOptions& options)
members.doc: Unwraps `faces`, or the whole mesh when empty, writing per-corner UVs.

members.name: BuildCharts
members.signature: static uint32_t BuildCharts(const FEditableMesh& mesh, const std::vector<uint32_t>& faces, float angleThresholdDegrees, std::vector<uint32_t>& outChartPerFace)
members.doc:
Charts alone, without touching the mesh — one entry per input face
giving its chart index. Exposed so the editor can colour islands and so
the charting can be tested apart from the packing.

members.name: MarkAngleSeams
members.signature: static uint32_t MarkAngleSeams(FEditableMesh& mesh, float angleThresholdDegrees)
members.doc:
Marks every edge whose dihedral angle exceeds the threshold as a seam,
so the user can see and then hand-edit what the charting would do.
